_comment: Named avatar attributes (skills), from https://anvilempires.wiki.gg/wiki/Avatar#Attributes. 'aliases' are other names players may type. 'levels' can hold a per-level table: [{"level": 1, "effect": "..."}, ...]. 'requirement_key' links to item requirements in the spreadsheet such as 'Melee 5'.
general: Named avatars have 6 attributes that increase by doing the related action.
Every named avatar rolls a maximum (cap) for each attribute, up to 10.
Experience comes from output: better equipment produces the same output faster, so you level faster.
Auxiliary avatars are capped at 1/1 and cannot train their attributes.

attributes.name: Fitness
attributes.effect: Longer sprint duration and more wounds before the avatar is incapacitated.
attributes.training: Sprint. Diagonal sprinting costs extra stamina, so sprinting in straight lines trains faster.

attributes.name: Melee Combat
attributes.effect: Decides which melee weapons and armour you can equip and how much damage you deal to creatures.
attributes.training: Deal damage with melee weapons - the total damage dealt counts. Overkill damage on NPCs still counts in full. The primary (stab) attack of spears trains Melee Combat.

attributes.name: Ranged Combat
attributes.effect: Decides which ranged weapons you can equip and how much damage you deal to creatures.
attributes.training: Deal damage with ranged weapons - the total damage dealt counts. Throwing a spear trains Ranged Combat.

attributes.name: Blacksmithing
attributes.effect: Fewer hammer strikes needed to forge items on an anvil.
attributes.training: Hit ingots on an Anvil or Stone Anvil. Early on, cold ingots on a Stone Anvil are the more efficient way to train.

attributes.name: Logging & Mining
attributes.effect: Less stamina used for harvesting, chopping trees, mining and breaking down ore.
attributes.training: Chop trees, mine and break down ore. The wiki's level table was measured by chopping trees; other methods may level at different rates.

attributes.name: Hunting
attributes.effect: Easier to move past animals without being noticed or attacked.
